title: Harborside Logistics — outreach scratch + objection flows
content:
Quick summary:
- Target: Harborside Logistics (regional 3PL + last-mile, ~650 employees). Suspect they run a mix of internal ops tools (Node/React) + legacy WMS; strong on telemetry + custom routing rules.
- Ask: pilot on improving agent-assisted dispatch + natural language SOP generation, plus an 'ops chat' to reduce phone triage.
- Hypothesis: Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) because of PII / location data; cost sensitivity but willing to commit for predictability.

Company background (raw intel):
- HQ: Charleston, SC; 12 regional hubs.
- M&A history: acquired two regional carriers in last 18 months -> integration pain points.
- CTO: Amanda Ribeiro (likely decision influencer). Head of Ops: Marco Diaz (day-to-day champion).
- Tech signals: references to "custom telemetry ingestion" at career page, APIs for GPS; likely uses Postgres + Redis + some ELK stack.

Why Redwood is a fit (quick bullet rationale):
- Private deployment for network/data isolation (compliance for shipping manifests).
- Dedicated capacity to guarantee low tail latency for live ops chat (SLOs matter).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated SOP prompts -> token cost savings for high-frequency queries.
- Rollouts + fallback helpful given multi-region hubs (can A/B at hub level).

Primary value props to emphasize (sales talk tracks):
1) Save ops time: 30–50% fewer phone escalations through contextual chat + structured outputs (action items, ETA updates).
2) Predictable economics: reserved capacity + token breakdowns -> predictable monthly run rate vs cloud burst surprises.
3) Integration velocity: runtime SDKs + sample adapter for common WMS APIs -> ship a pilot in 6–8 weeks.
4) Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller quantized model if Dedicated pool hits pressure (keeps UI alive).

Stakeholder map (rough):
- Amanda Ribeiro, CTO (security, architecture, procurement gate)
- Marco Diaz, Head of Ops (champion, wants immediate ops wins)
- Priya Shah, Director Customer Experience (wants fewer delayed ETAs)
- Legal: contracts + SOC2 / export controls (will push for Private/VPC)
- Procurement: pricing conversation / commitment length

Decision criteria we need to surface early:
- Data residency / isolation requirement? (on-prem vs VPC)
- Latency SLOs for chat (95th percentile target)
- Integration points: which WMS / TMS (ask for API docs early)
- Volume profile: concurrent agents, messages/day, message length distribution

Objections (anticipated) + quick counters (talking points):
- "We can't justify spend right now" -> counter: propose a narrow three-hub pilot with reserved micro-capacity, show modeled run-rate with observed caching uplift -> run a 6-week ROI dashboard.
- "We already have an internal chatbot PoC" -> counter: internal PoC lacks production-grade inference/runtime + model ops. Emphasize rollouts, dedicated pools, cost per token visibility, and support for function/tool-calling to connect to their systems.
- "Security/legal concerns about manifests/addresses" -> counter: offer Private deployment + KMS integration and audit logs. Provide previous redacted SOC2 artifact and data flow diagram.
- "Latency spikes during peak" -> counter: show autoscaling + fallback model variant plan; pricing for burst capacity and dedicated threshold rules.

Outreach sequence (first pass) — tailored, short, human: 
1) Email 1 (warm intro to Amanda + Marco): one para, reference acquisition pain + ops examples, ask to run a short pilot (3 hubs). Subject candidates: "Reduce dispatch triage by 30% at Harborside" / "Quick pilot idea: ops chat + SOP auto-gen for Harborside"
2) If no response in 4 days -> short nudge to Marco with 2 bullets: 1) expected win (less phone time), 2) low-setup pilot (6–8 weeks).
3) Call script (30m discovery): 7 mins intros, 10 mins current flows + costs, 8 mins demo of Redwood-hosted sample (mocked with Harborside data), 5 mins next steps.

Call/demo talking points (messy):
- Start with a live scenario: "package delayed at hub — what's the ops flow?" capture pain, hand off to Redwood flow: show structured ETA message + SOP.
- Emphasize tokens -> show caching savings example: repeated address normalization and SOP templates stored in KV cache reduces token rates 45% in similar pilots.
- Show how rollouts can test smaller model in non-critical routes.

Quick email template (scratch):
Subject: Pilot idea — reduce dispatch phone time at Harborside
Hi Amanda / Marco,
I noticed Harborside has been integrating two carriers recently — that often creates extra triage time for dispatch. We built a small pilot for a 3-hub rollout that uses an ops chat + SOP generation to cut phone escalations and speed ETA updates. Low lift on your side, Private or Dedicated options. Interested in 20 minutes to walk through the plan?
— Ethan

Data & measurement (what I'd commit to show in pilot):
- Baseline metrics: avg call duration, tickets per hub, phone escalations/day, mean time to update ETA
- Pilot metrics: reduction in escalations, mean handle time via chat, accuracy of SOP suggestions (manual review %), cost per resolved issue, latency (p50/p95).
- Weekly dashboard: tokens consumed, cache hit rate, route-by-route latency.

Integration checklist (questions to ask early):
- Do you have API for shipment status updates? (pull vs push)
- How are user identities mapped between WMS and customer support? (need stable IDs for caching)
- Any PII redaction requirements? retention windows?
- Peak windows (weekday/off-hour patterns) — helps sizing Dedicated pool.

Risks / red flags (notes to self):
- They might insist on on-prem; ops budget for on-prem will be 3x baseline, need to price accordingly.
- Legal may demand no third-party hosting of full manifests — will push for field-level redaction and Private deployment.
- Potential internal politics: Head of Ops likes quick wins; CTO wants architecture control — need both in briefing deck.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Find HAR-API docs (ask Marco for endpoints) — DATA REQUEST email draft prepared.
- Build pilot SOW outline (6–8 weeks, 3 hubs, success criteria) — due EOD Thursday.
- Prep short demo dataset (sanitized manifests) — ask solutions-eng for sample transformation script.
- Schedule intro call: aim for week of Nov 18 (Amanda + Marco) — add Maya to invite.

Notes to self / unresolved:
- Confirm whether Harborside's TLS termination is customer-managed (affects Private design).
- Pricing sensitivity: what is their monthly software budget for Ops tools? 15–25k/mo? Need to validate.
- Draft 2nd email variant focusing on CX (Priya) instead of Ops for parallel outreach.

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Offer "dispatch flash" feature: quick one-click runbook generation from incident description (could be 1–2 hero feature for pitch).
- Use anomaly detection telemetry to trigger automated SOP suggestions before escalation.

--- end scratch ---
